To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a multidisciplinary approach is needed to treat patients with differentiated thyroid cancer.
The follow up of patients with differentiated thyroid carcinoma should be performed in accordance with the international guidelines.
1. The follow-up of differentiated thyroid cancer patients should be performed by a multidisciplinary team
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model to predict the evolution of thyroid cancer.
the development of a new class of models for the treatment of patients with thyroid cancer.
the development of a model of the dynamics of the thyroid carcinoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

patients with differentiated thyroid carcinoma should be followed up by an experienced endocrinologist and/or nuclear physician in collaboration with a multidisciplinary team, which should include an anatomic pathologist, a cytologist, a surgeon and a medical imaging expert.

the follow-up should be individualized according to the clinical and histological features of the tumor, and should include a combination of clinical examination and serum thyroglobulin (Tg) measurement, neck ultrasonography and, when necessary, radioiodine whole body scanning.

the patient with differentiated thyroid cancer should be followed up in a multidisciplinary team, including endocrinologists, nuclear medicine specialists, head and neck surgeons, cytopathologists, anatomopathologists, general physicians and nursing personnel, with the aim to achieve the highest negative predictive value in order to avoid unnecessary diagnostic procedures and the highest sensitivity in order to detect the persistence/recurrence of disease as early as possible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the follow up of patients with differentiated thyroid carcinoma (DTC) should be performed in a multidisciplinary setting.

the thyroid cancer follow-up protocol should have a high predictive negative value in order to exclude patients from useless diagnostic procedures and a high sensitivity, sufficient to identify early recurrence of the disease.
we found no evidence of an increased risk of cancer among women with a history of thyroid cancer who were exposed to radioactive iodine for the treatment of Graves disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the absence of any other information, the presence of a single, small, low-intermediate-risk, well-differentiated thyroid carcinoma should not lead to a recommendation for adjuvant radioactive iodine therapy, even in the setting of a large, multicenter, randomized trial.
, although the risk of recurrence in the first 10 years is low in differentiated thyroid cancer, the risk of recurrence increases after 10 years.

, in the absence of a consensus on the definition of the optimal follow-up protocol in patients with differentiated thyroid carcinoma, the decision to perform or not to perform a follow-up should be made by the patient and the physician on an individual basis, taking into account the clinical and histological characteristics of the tumor and the individual risk of relapse, and the possible benefits of follow-up.
